title: Andee puts its payment limits in code a prompt cannot reach
summary: A phone agent whose limits live in code a prompt cannot reach. Andee never enters a payment password and won't let a stranger's notification open its vault, because the refusal is coded into its dispatcher rather than its prompt: https://github.com/kuafuai/andee
body_markdown:
An agent that reads your screen can be handed instructions by whatever is on it, such as a web page, a notification or a message from a stranger, and a model that treats them as part of its prompt may follow them. Andee, an on-device agent for Android and macOS from kuafuai/andee, answers that with a design choice I want to see in more agents: the hard limits live in the dispatcher rather than in the prompt.

So a stranger's notification cannot open Andee's vault or grant it new permissions, and a page that tells it to enter a payment password does not get its way. That refusal does not depend on the model choosing to refuse.

## Lines it will not cross

Andee fills a page up to the last button and leaves that button to you. It stops before the final confirmation of a purchase and never enters a payment password. The ready-made "cancel my subscriptions" scene shows the pattern: it reads your subscriptions, puts the monthly total on top, then goes one at a time with Cancel, Keep or Think about it, and stops before each final confirm.

The ready-made message-watching scene is also cautious with untrusted input. It reads the notification shade across chat apps, reports the ones that need you in one line each, keeps groups, newsletters and ads quiet, and names a stranger's link or verification code as suspicious without touching it.

Device pairing follows the same idea. Pair two devices by QR code and the Andee on each can ask the other for help, such as your phone handing a coding job to your Mac. A friend can also be somebody else's Andee. In that case its owner is asked before anything happens, and the work runs where it cannot see your memory, your conversations or your vault.

## A guard rail learned the hard way

My favourite detail is a measured failure. On a HONOR phone with WeChat 8.0.80, reading and screenshotting WeChat worked fine, but the very first accessibility-injected tap made WeChat protect its own window. Screenshots then went black for the user too, not just for Andee, and stayed that way across a force-stop. Only clearing WeChat's data and logging in again recovered it.

So the phone build refuses tap, long-press, swipe, type and submit before sending them while WeChat is in front. Reads and system back and home still work. That guard comes from an incident the project measured on a real phone.

## How it sees and acts

Andee needs nothing from the apps it drives. It reads the accessibility tree and a screenshot, and aims on a labelled grid instead of doing coordinate maths, which the project calls the thing general models are worst at. The brain runs against any OpenAI-compatible model you choose. Its memory of you is marked `localOnly`, filtered out of the hub payload, and listed in a "What it remembers" screen where every entry can be deleted. The project says the only data it sends to its authors is a version number and a phone model during update checks.

The project describes Andee in personal terms, as a resident of the device with its own character, six looks and nineteen moods, biased toward staying silent. You can take or leave that part. The dispatcher-level limits are useful either way.

## Before you install

The recommended route is a one-click build on CodeFlying, a separate service with its own terms and pricing, which ships the package with model and voice keys configured and gives new accounts a free allowance. Release packages from GitHub carry no keys, so you can choose On-device and enter your own model and voice keys instead. On Android you grant Overlay and then Accessibility. On a Mac you allow Accessibility and Screen Recording. I would start with the message-watching scene, which only reads, and test whether a planted instruction in a notification gets flagged.
